_meta.purpose: Multi-hop / cross-source retrieval eval (Track 2 of the memory-orchestration cycle). The RULER that gates every Track-3 retrieval change (rerank, IDF rank, entity layer, vectors). Each query's correct answer requires evidence from >=2 cards in >=2 provenance sources, connected by a shared bridge concept (tag).

format.q: natural-language question phrased around the BRIDGE concept + one card's specifics (HotpotQA-style); the 2nd expected card is reached via the shared bridge tag (graph expansion), not by trivially naming both
format.expect: array of >=2 card id-substrings (matched with .includes(), case-insensitive, like real-retrieval-eval.json)
format.sources: the provenance families the expected cards come from (seed=real-callout-seed, workflow=workflow-knowledge-jsonl, auto=auto-memory:pi-memory)
format.bridge: the shared concept tag that SHOULD connect the expected cards (the multi-hop edge under test)
format.why: 1-line rationale why BOTH cards are needed

_meta.designNotes: seed<->workflow dominates the cross-source edges because that is where genuine same-concept pairs exist in the current 449-card vault; a few seed<->auto pairs test the auto-memory axis. The eval is deliberately HARD: a single-hop tag-match retriever finds cards matching query tokens, but the 2nd expected card often does NOT share the query tokens — it shares only the bridge tag. Surfacing it requires graph/tag expansion. A future entity layer (Track 3.3) must beat the deterministic baseline (scripts/multi-hop-measure.mjs) by >=+0.10 set-recall@4 to ship.
_meta.gate: Track 3 levers must beat this set's baseline by >=+0.10 mean set-recall@4, or retire with a receipt (same discipline as iter-7).
_meta.leakageCaveat: FLAW FOUND in Track 3.4 (2026-07-11): this eval set LEAKS answer vocabulary — 11/15 queries contain >=30% of BOTH expected cards' tokens (e.g. the 'help-text-advertises' query shares 10/11 tokens with card 1 and 9/11 with card 2). Consequence: any CONTENT-based retriever (vectors nomic +0.433 -> 1.0, or full-text) trivially aces it; the tag-path (0.567) looks weak only because tags can't exploit the leaked vocabulary. So this set is INVALID for judging content-based multi-hop levers. BEFORE re-measuring vectors/full-text, REDESIGN: queries must mention ONLY one expected card's vocabulary + the bridge concept ABSTRACTLY, so the 2nd card is findable only via the bridge. The tag-path baseline (0.567) and rerank (3.1) are less affected (tags don't hold the leaked vocab) but still ride on this flawed set.

baseline.read: fullRecall@4=0.333 is the headline: the tag-path fully answers only 1/3 of multi-hop queries. bridgeLift plateaus at K=8 (some 2nd cards are in the pool but under-ranked -> rerank lever; others are rank=null, NOT in the pool at all -> tag-path NL weakness, P7). The entity layer (Track 3.3) must beat setRecall@4 by >=+0.10 vs this 0.567 baseline.
